bill.title: Export Control Enforcement and Enhancement Act
bill.latestActionText: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
bill.officialSummary: Export Control Enforcement and Enhancement Act This bill allows for expedited consideration of modifications to the Entity List. (The Entity List is managed by the Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security. The list identifies the names of persons who are involved, or have the potential to be involved, in activities contrary to U.S. national security or foreign policy interests.) Specifically, the bill allows any member of the End-User Review Committee to submit proposals directly to the full committee requesting a vote for additions to, removals from, or other modifications with respect to the Entity List. Generally, within 30 days of receiving a proposal, the committee must vote to approve or disapprove the proposal. Generally, the bill establishes a presumption of denial for a license application to export, reexport, or in-country transfer controlled items that involves a foreign person added to the Entity List under the authorities provided by this bill.

classification.plainSummary: This bill speeds up the process for adding or removing companies and individuals from the Entity List, a government roster of foreign persons whose activities may threaten U.S. national security or foreign policy. It allows any member of a review committee to propose changes directly for a vote, which must generally occur within 30 days. The bill also creates a default policy of denying export licenses for controlled items when the recipient was added to the Entity List under these new procedures.

industries.rationale: Technology companies face direct regulatory obligations when exporting semiconductors, software, and other controlled items subject to Entity List restrictions.
Defense and aerospace manufacturers export controlled military and dual-use technologies that are subject to Entity List licensing requirements.
Manufacturers of industrial equipment and dual-use goods must comply with export controls when shipping to Entity List persons.

plain.whatItDoes: This bill would allow for expedited consideration of modifications to the Entity List.
plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who buys imported goods, and people who make goods here.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in prices, and what is made where. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
